content:
A few months ago, the MacBook Neo made a strong debut as the best value-for-money laptop of 2026. Despite a recent price increase, it remains the easiest entry-level laptop to recommend for most people. Like other Apple products offering great value, this laptop also comes in several eye-catching colours, including citrus yellow, blush pink, indigo and silver, adding a touch of personality and colour to the MacBook lineup. However, my one gripe is that most MacBook accessories still come in the traditional matching silver or space grey. For this reason, Satechi has launched three brand-new colour-matching accessories...

I previously reviewed the 'big brother' version of this product and absolutely loved it. This is the most versatile accessory in Satechi's new product line. It expands one of your USB-C ports into 5 additional ports, and it's extremely compact — about the size of a puck, with built-in MagSafe. So you can use it with both your MacBook Neo and iPhone at the same time. This USB-C hub offers the following features:

  • HDMI output, supporting up to 4K 60Hz video
  • USB-C pass-through charging, supporting up to 60W
  • USB-C port, supporting up to 5Gbps transfer speeds
  • USB-A port, supporting up to 5Gbps transfer speeds
  • Full-size SD card reader
  • A high-quality nylon-braided USB-C cable

Since this product comes with MagSafe, the manufacturer includes a magnetic ring that can be attached to the lid of your MacBook Neo. Even better, the metal ring's colour perfectly matches your Neo! Even when not using the hub, this magnetic ring won't look out of place. As mentioned earlier, this is my personal favourite product — extremely versatile. It's compact, well-made, covers the main ports most people need, and works with a wide variety of devices.

The OntheGo multi-port adapter is available in the same colours as the MacBook Neo, and goes on sale today at Amazon and the Satechi official website for US$44.99.

This is the more familiar, traditional USB-C hub form factor that everyone knows. It snaps directly onto the side of the MacBook Neo (hence the name 'Snap hub'), giving you six new ports at once — one more than the OntheGo hub mentioned above. From how snugly it fits once attached, you can tell this product was designed specifically for the MacBook Neo. The Snap Hub offers the following features:

  • SD and MicroSD card readers
  • USB-C pass-through charging, supporting up to 45W (enough to charge the MacBook Neo, since the Neo only charges at a maximum of 30W)

The Snap Hub is undoubtedly the most seamlessly integrated of the three accessories in appearance — both in look and feel, it looks like it came from Apple itself. It features a two-tone design, with the top perfectly matching the Neo's material and colour, while the rest of the body is cleverly made from soft-touch rubber, because the manufacturer knows the hub will be sitting right against the Neo's metal body, and metal-on-metal contact usually doesn't work well. I think this is an excellent design choice. One thing to note is that this hub will occupy two of the Neo's USB-C ports, but the hub itself...

The USB-C Snap Hub goes on sale today, available in the same four colours as the Neo mentioned earlier. It's priced at US$44.99, the same as the OntheGo hub adapter, and is available at Amazon and the Satechi official website.

To round out Satechi's brand-new Neo product line, they've redesigned the Slim EX mouse, releasing it in colours that match the rest of their products. I previously tried the non-coloured version of this mouse, and it's one of the products I most frequently recommend — incredible value for money. For just US$29, you get:

  • Connect to up to 3 different devices simultaneously — two via Bluetooth, one via a 2.4GHz receiver (and it's a USB-C receiver!)
  • Aluminium alloy housing
  • Charges via USB-C
  • User-replaceable batteries
  • Up to three months of continuous use, with over a year of battery life in standby mode
  • A USB-C cable included for charging and connectivity

The build quality and feel of this mouse is absolutely on par with products costing twice as much. It has a low-profile aluminium body that feels great to the touch, while also being ergonomically designed for extended use. Switching quickly between multiple devices is second nature for me — constantly going back and forth between my MacBook and iPad. Plus, the 2.4GHz receiver uses USB-C instead of USB-A, which is absolutely an underrated upgrade. Although the Neo's trackpad is already excellent, I personally use both a trackpad and a mouse at the same time. The trackpad for gestures and lateral...

The Slim EX wireless mouse is available in the same four colours mentioned earlier, as well as the previously released black version. The mouse is priced at US$29.99 and is now available at Amazon and the Satechi official website. If you want to save a bit, the black version is actually the same mouse and is currently on sale for just US$23.99.

Summary

Satechi is the first brand to launch colour-matching accessories for the MacBook Neo, and they clearly understand their target audience. They've brought high-quality, feature-rich accessories to the MacBook Neo lineup, making up for some of the cost-cutting measures taken to hit that US$699 price point. All of these accessories are well-made, packed with useful features, and enhance the MacBook Neo experience.

If I had to pick just one, I'd lean slightly toward the OntheGo multi-port adapter, purely because it's so versatile and works with any device equipped with a USB-C port and MagSafe. That said, the physical integration of the Snap Hub with the Neo is equally impressive, and the Slim EX mouse is the perfect finishing touch to the entire product line. What do you think? Are these accessories worth picking up? Does colour-matching matter to you? Feel free to leave a comment below and let's discuss!
